title: Modern Jesuits unashamed: Costerus, Salazar, de Argento—maternal power over Christ; Mary as Domina Dei
source_text: LXVI. Nec etiam istorum recentiores pudet. Testis sit Franciscus Costerus Jesuita, qui sic Virginem alloquitur, Alii omnes precantur ut servi; tu ut mater authoritatem habens, exaudiris pro tua reverentia. Item, Quid enim est matrem esse Dei? mater causa est filii; mater est superior filio; matri debetur honor a filio; matri tenetur morem gerere filius. Testis sit quoque Jesuita Salazar, cui constare videtur Virginem sanctissimam patriam in filium potestatem obtinuisse, ne quid universalem ejus ditionem efugeret. Et Mariam jure materno, quadam supra Christum potestate regia fuisse gavisam. Atque adeo Christum Deum & hominem, fuisse aliquid illius proprium, sub illius patria potestate & quasi Dominio constitutum, non alio modo quam alios filios. Neque enim verisimile esse ratione divinitatis, cui humana natura erat sociata, Christum a patria potestate emancipatum fuisse, quam alii parentes jure naturali obtinent in filios. Quin putat hoc jus etiamnum apud Sanctam Virginem manere, illamque eo adhuc saepius uti. Sane, inquit, Virgo Sanctissima hoc jure & potestate sua saepius usa est: Sed tum maxime, quum apud filium pro nobis intercedit. Testis denique sit P. de Argento etiam ipse Jesuita, cujus ista verba citantur de Beata Virgine, Quasi sexus conditionis oblita, in filium Dominium suscipiens, supra ipsum Dei thronum solium suum collocavit. Et hic praeterea, quibus sentire se & nunc adhuc Mariae servire, Domine Jesu Salvator amabilissime permitte me aliquid matri tuae praestare. Et si non vis hoc mihi credere saltem permitte te, ut dum matri tuae servis ego serviam tibi. Unde est quod inter Beatae Virginis excellentias hunc titulum ponit, quod sit Domina Dei. Haec est, inquit, suprema Beatissimae Virginis dignitas; Haec summa & adoranda ejus potestas, ut Deus subjiciatur illi & ipsa in illum Dominium habeat.
pass_a_gloss: Nor are even more recent men of those ashamed. Let Francis Costerus the Jesuit be witness, who thus addresses the Virgin: All others pray as servants; thou as mother having authority art heard for thy reverence. Likewise, For what is it to be mother of God? a mother is cause of the son; a mother is superior to the son; honor is owed to a mother from the son; a son is bound to humor a mother. Let the Jesuit Salazar also be witness, to whom it seems clear that the most holy Virgin obtained paternal power over the son, lest anything escape her universal rule. And that Mary by maternal right enjoyed a certain royal power above Christ. And so that Christ God and man was something proper to her, constituted under her paternal power and as it were Dominion, in no other way than other sons. For it is not likely that by reason of divinity, with which human nature was associated, Christ was emancipated from the paternal power which other parents obtain by natural right over sons. Nay he thinks this right still remains with the Holy Virgin, and that she still uses it rather often. Truly, he says, the most Holy Virgin has rather often used this her right and power: But then especially, when she intercedes with her son for us. Finally let Father de Argento, also himself a Jesuit, be witness, whose these words are cited of the Blessed Virgin: As if forgetful of the condition of sex, taking up Dominion over the son, she placed her throne above the very throne of God. And here besides, by which he feels that he still even now serves Mary: Lord Jesus most lovable Savior, permit me to furnish something to thy mother. And if thou wilt not believe this of me, at least permit thyself, that while thou servest thy mother I may serve thee. Whence it is that among the excellencies of the Blessed Virgin he places this title, that she is Lady of God. This is, he says, the supreme dignity of the most Blessed Virgin; This her highest and adorable power, that God is subjected to her and she herself has Dominion over Him.
pass_b_english: Recent Jesuits double down: Costerus—mother heard by authority, not as a servant.
Salazar: lasting maternal/royal power over Christ, used especially when she intercedes.
De Argento: throne above God’s; title Domina Dei—God subjected to her dominion.

choices.english: that God be subjected to her
choices.why: De Argento’s climax Le Blanc records.
